claims.text: High-entropy alloys with tailored chemical short-range order can exhibit enhanced superconducting properties.
Optimizing lattice thermal conductivity through chemical short-range-order tailoring enhances superconducting properties.
Optimizing magnetic behavior through chemical short-range-order tailoring enhances superconducting properties.
Chemical short-range order, lattice thermal conductivity, and magnetic behavior mediate the proposed superconducting enhancement.
Optimized microstructure design leads to enhanced superconducting properties.
Tailoring the high-entropy alloy will produce a higher superconducting critical temperature than the untailored alloy.
Tailoring the high-entropy alloy will produce a higher superconducting current density than the untailored alloy.
The exact mechanisms behind high coercive fields are not yet fully understood.
The relationship between chemical short-range order and thermal conductivity is not yet fully understood.
